title: Manifold Sampling via Entropy Maximization
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: Baseline samplers misallocate mass across disconnected feasible components, while ours matches the ground-truth distribution.
layout: 2x5 grid of scatter panels, methods as columns, ground truth rightmost
description: A 2x5 grid of small scatter plots. Columns are labeled NHR, OLLA, SCMC, MASEM-NHR (Ours), and Ground Truth. The top row, 'Sine', shows a damped sine curve as a black line, with a dashed horizontal line and a green shaded feasible region above it. Blue dots mark the samples. The bottom row, 'Disconnected Disks', shows a large black circle containing two small dashed-outline green disks of different sizes, with blue dots scattered inside them. NHR and OLLA cluster dots in the small disk and the tallest sine peak, and undersample the large disk and the leftmost peak. SCMC scatters dots outside the feasible disks. The MASEM and Ground Truth columns look nearly identical, with mass spread proportionally. The eye goes first to the right-hand columns, for comparison.
caption: Scatter plots of 100 samples from different samplers on synthetic benchmarks. Black lines show equality constraints, and green shaded areas mark the feasible region(s) by inequality constraints. The bottom row depicts 3d samples on spheres projected into 2d. NHR and OLLA fail to allocate correct sample masses: the larger disk and the leftmost peak of the sine are undersampled.
abstract: Sampling from constrained distributions has a wide range of applications, including in Bayesian optimization and robotics. Prior work establishes convergence and feasibility guarantees for constrained sampling, but assumes that the feasible set is connected. However, in practice, the feasible set often decomposes into multiple disconnected components, which makes efficient sampling under constraints challenging. In this paper, we propose MAnifold Sampling via Entropy Maximization (MASEM) for uniform sampling on a manifold with an unknown number of disconnected components, implicitly defined by smooth equality and inequality constraints. The presented method uses a resampling scheme to maximize the entropy of the empirical distribution based on k-nearest neighbor density estimation. We show that, in the mean field, MASEM decreases the KL-divergence between the empirical distribution and the maximum-entropy target exponentially in the number of resampling steps. We instantiate MASEM with multiple local samplers and demonstrate its versatility and efficiency on synthetic and robotics-based benchmarks. MASEM enables fast and scalable mixing across a range of constrained sampling problems, improving over alternatives by an order of magnitude in Sinkhorn distance with competitive runtime.
